author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown left Wednesday night’s season opener in Seattle with a right ankle injury during the third quarter.

Brown was targeted by quarterback Drake Maye on third down when Seahawks nickel cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett deflected the pass. Pritchett’s knee landed on the outside of Brown’s ankle as the receiver went to the turf, Reuters reported. Brown walked off, removed his right cleat and entered the sideline medical tent.

The Patriots initially listed him as questionable to return. He did not rejoin the offense when a roughing-the-punter penalty extended the possession. Brown had three receptions for a team-high 26 yards in the first half.

New England acquired Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in an early-June trade, making his availability an important early-season issue for the passing game. The initial report did not include a diagnosis, imaging result or recovery timeline. Any assessment beyond a right ankle injury would therefore be premature until the team provides a medical update.
dek: Brown walked off during New England’s first possession of the second half in Seattle and was initially listed as questionable to return.
headline: Patriots receiver A.J. Brown leaves opener with right ankle injury
